summary: Pre-output idle period for chat completions following runtime+model cutover causing elevated TTFB
description: Issue summary: BrightAssist reported a pronounced pre-output idle period for chat completions (high TTFB) immediately after our 2026-03-09 runtime and model cutover. Impact: customer-facing latency increases causing UI timeouts and degraded UX for interactive assistants. Environment: prod-us-west cluster serving BrightAssist's dedicated pool after runtime v2.14 and model rw-chat-7B-q4 repin. Observed since 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send a chat completion request to /v1/chat/completions against BrightAssist dedicated endpoint (prod-us-west) with a 4-turn context and max_tokens=256.
2) Request streaming=true and measure time between request and first token chunk (TTFB).
3) Repeat across 10 requests; observe variability with median ~450ms pre-cutover vs 2.8s post-cutover and p95 > 6s.
4) Toggle model pin to previous model build and observe TTFB change.
5) Force request route to bypass routing affinity (fast-path) and compare.
observed_behavior: After the cutover there is a consistent pre-output idle period: median TTFB increased from ~0.45s to ~2.8s and p95 jumped to >6s. Traffic then occasionally times out at the client (client-side 10s). Token stream arrives normally after the idle period; subsequent token emission rate is unchanged.
expected_behavior: TTFB should remain within prior baseline (p50 < 600ms, p95 < 1.2s) for BrightAssist dedicated pool when model pinned to rw-chat-7B-q4 and runtime v2.14.

investigation_notes:
2026-03-10 02:00 UTC - Initial triage by Support (Ava): confirmed BrightAssist reports and collected traces and p50/p95 metrics.
2026-03-10 03:20 UTC - Eng (Ravi) reproduced in staging by replaying traffic; reproduced only when routing selected nodes with new kernel-quant dispatch.
Hypothesis A: new runtime build introduced an additional synchronous KV cache validation step that blocks streaming until cache warmup finishes for some model variants. Evidence: serve_prepare_kv_cache durations correlated tightly with TTFB jumps (R=0.87).
Hypothesis B: route affinity change caused requests to land on nodes with cold model shards requiring slow model_init_check (consistent with model_init_check log durations of 600-1200ms).
Correlations: high TTFB aligns with nodes running kernel-quant v3.2 and compiled model variant rw-chat-7B-q4-q.
Observability: Console traces and per-token breakdown show the idle period occurs before stream_start is emitted to client. No 5xxs seen on server; client received 200 then delayed chunk stream.
Next steps: instrument blocking points (KV priming, compatibility check) with finer-grained spans and add sampling for nodes running kernel-quant v3.2.
mitigation: Applied temporary routing override at 2026-03-10 08:45 UTC to prefer fast-path nodes (bypass kernel-quant v3.2) for BrightAssist pool. Customer reverted to previous model pin (rw-chat-7B-q4@build-20260301) via support guidance which restored TTFB to baseline. Monitoring set up to track regressions.
resolution: Workaround in place (routing override + model repin). Root cause still under active investigation. ENG follow-up task created to remove synchronous KV validation and make priming async (INT-678). We will release a non-blocking cache priming patch in next runtime micro-release and validate with canaries before global rollout.
